description:
REVIEWED 2026-10-25 (TodoReview) against origin/develop 9a184b619 and fork main ea44bcc9 (30.24.0.13). PROBLEM
Two tests were seen failing once or twice each on PR CI under `-n` parallel runs and pass alone: tests/unit/core/tpch/test_tpch_generator.py `TestDataOrganizationConfig::test_default_none` (asserts `_data_organization_config is None`) and tests/unit/utils/test_config_interface.py `TestConfigProviderRegistration::test_default_provider_is_the_simple_one` (asserts the process provider is `SimpleConfigProvider`). Each is a VICTIM of process-global state set by an earlier test on the same xdist worker.

VERIFIED FACTS (2026-10-25, code read on origin/develop; no failing log has been captured in this item)
- What each victim reads: TPCHDataGenerator.__init__ (benchbox/core/tpch/generator.py) reads env `BENCHBOX_DATA_ORGANIZATION_CONFIG_JSON` when no kwarg is given; `get_config_provider()` returns the module global `benchbox.utils.config_interface._config_provider`.
- Who sets them: `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py` writes `os.environ[DATA_ORGANIZATION_ENV]` (about line 899); `benchbox/cli/app.py` calls `install_cli_config_provider` (line 90); the test `test_installing_the_cli_provider_makes_it_the_process_provider` installs a CLI provider itself.
- Isolation that already exists: commit cce8a9de0 (#2530, 2026-10-02) added `_hermetic_state`, tests/conftest.py `_reset_global_config_provider` (restores `_config_provider` after every test) and tests/unit/conftest.py `_owned_cli_invocations`, which wraps `CliRunner.invoke` and restores the provider, `printing._QUIET`, logging and the two env keys `BENCHBOX_NON_INTERACTIVE` and `BENCHBOX_DATA_ORGANIZATION_CONFIG_JSON`; a leak is meant to fail the LEAKING test. So the two obvious leak paths are guarded for in-process CliRunner use; the failures therefore come through a path that guard does not cover (candidates, all unverified: tests calling the click/app entry point or `run` internals directly instead of CliRunner, threads or atexit callbacks that outlive a test, subprocess-free `os.environ` writes in `patch.dict` that exit late, a plugin ordering issue between the autouse fixtures). Do not assume any of them.
- The two files are not in the same package, so the leaker is a third test.

DECISION GATES (stop and ask the owner)
G1 If the leak is in a test owned elsewhere: fix that test (recommended). Adding a broader autouse reset is acceptable only if the #2530 leak detector still fails the leaker; never disable or relax the detector.
G2 If the only available remedy is a retry, flaky marker, xfail or skip: stop and ask (the repository forbids SKIP/rerun-to-green).

GUARDRAILS
- No `pytest.mark.flaky`, reruns, xfail, skips, `--no-verify`, or timeout bumps as a fix.
- Do not edit tests/conftest.py guards to make the symptom disappear; do not touch `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` or `make test-unlock`.
- One heavy run at a time; use `make test-fast` or targeted `uv run -- python -m pytest <paths> -n 4`.

STANDING GUARDRAILS: work only in a `make worktree-create` worktree after `make agent-write-preflight` (primary clone /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox is read-only); run tests only through make targets (`make test-fast`, `make pr-preflight`, `make sql-execution-gate`, `make tpcds-obt-equivalence`) or targeted `uv run -- python -m pytest <paths> -n 4`; never BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR, `make test-unlock` or raw broad runs; one heavy run at a time; no live-cloud spend and no production publish without explicit owner approval; published result bundles are never edited (only manifest-sidecar `known_defects` and results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md per results-data/DEFECTIVE_DATAGEN_AUDIT.md); no SKIP / --no-verify / `git add -A`; no explanatory comments or docstrings in code (`make comment-policy-check`); uv only; identity Joe Harris, no Co-Authored-By; PR flow `make pr-preflight` once, `make pr-open`, CI + oracle review, `make pr-arm`. Stop and ask the owner on unexpected result changes, relaxed guards, oracle stand-ins or real design choices.
